Article 4 (Office for Metropolitan Transportation Policy)
(1) The Director of the Office for Metropolitan Transportation Policy shall be a general civil servant belonging to the senior civil service grade, with a job grade of grade 2.
(2) The Office for Metropolitan Transportation Policy shall have the following departments: the Department of Metropolitan Transportation Policy, the Department of Metropolitan Bus, and the Department of Metropolitan Transportation Economics. Each department head shall be a deputy director, a scientific and technological officer, or a clerk. <Amended February 22, 2022, August 30, 2023>
(3) The head of the Department of Metropolitan Transportation Policy shall be responsible for the following matters: <Amended February 22, 2022>
1. Overall management and coordination of metropolitan transportation policies
2. Support for the development of the basic plan for metropolitan transportation
3. Development and implementation of the implementation plan for metropolitan transportation
4. Matters related to the development of annual implementation plans and review of implementation results for the implementation plan for metropolitan transportation
5. Development and implementation of measures to improve metropolitan transportation
5.2. Development and implementation of special measures for metropolitan transportation
5.3. Designation and revocation of special measures areas for metropolitan transportation
6. Matters related to the operation and improvement of the metropolitan transportation facility burden system
7. Matters related to the use plan for metropolitan transportation facility burden
8. Matters related to the designation of metropolitan transportation facilities

Items:
9. Matters regarding the linkage and functional division of regional transportation facilities in metropolitan areas.
10. Matters regarding conflict management related to the regional transportation system in metropolitan areas.
11. Designation of regional transportation axes for metropolitan areas.
11.2. Matters regarding the preparation of regional transportation measures for each transportation axis.
11.3. Matters regarding the establishment and operation of regional transportation-related consultation bodies for each metropolitan area.
12. Matters regarding the management of regional transportation demand in metropolitan areas.
13. Matters regarding the agenda setting and post-management of the Metropolitan Area Regional Transportation Committee (hereinafter referred to as "the Committee"), the practical committee under Article 9(4) of the Act, and the regional committee under Article 9(5) of the Act.
14. International cooperation work related to regional transportation policies in metropolitan areas.
15. Support for super-regional cooperation in the field of regional transportation in metropolitan areas.
16. Matters regarding the adjustment of the scope of metropolitan areas.
17. Matters regarding the establishment of a regional transportation system for achieving carbon neutrality.
④ The Director of the Regional Bus Division is responsible for the following:
1. Regional express and direct bus services (hereinafter referred to as "regional buses") in metropolitan areas.

1. Overall planning and implementation of the route system.
1.2. Overall coordination and management of policies such as regional bus operations within metropolitan areas.
1.3. Matters related to feasibility assessments and the operation of route committees for establishing new regional bus routes within metropolitan areas.
1.4. Matters related to conflict resolution concerning the operation of regional buses within metropolitan areas.
2. Matters related to the approval and registration of changes to business plans for regional bus transportation within metropolitan areas.
3. Matters related to the establishment and implementation of vehicle supply plans for regional bus transportation within metropolitan areas.
3.2. Operation of evaluation committees for selecting regional bus transportation operators within metropolitan areas.
4. Matters related to the licensing of regional buses within metropolitan areas.
5. Matters related to the approval and registration of transportation terms and amendments for regional bus transportation operators within metropolitan areas.
6. Supervision and oversight of regional bus transportation operators within metropolitan areas.
7. Matters related to the introduction and support of public-private partnerships for regional buses within metropolitan areas.
8. Matters related to establishing an integrated network connecting regional bus and local bus routes within metropolitan areas.
9. Matters related to the management and support of labor relations within metropolitan areas.
10. Matters related to regional bus transportation within metropolitan areas.

11. Matters related to the operation and safety management of large-scale public transportation vehicles and facilities within metropolitan areas.
12. Matters related to the management and optimization of large-scale public transportation vehicle increases and decreases.
13. Matters related to the management of large-scale public transportation reservation systems.
14. Matters related to the expansion and support of environmentally friendly and large-capacity large-scale public transportation.
15. Matters related to the management and service evaluation of operators and transportation companies of large-scale public transportation within metropolitan areas.
16. Investigation, analysis, and statistical management of the status of large-scale public transportation within metropolitan areas.
17. Development and improvement of policies and systems to enhance the convenience of mobility for individuals with disabilities who use large-scale public transportation within metropolitan areas.
18. Establishment and operation of an integrated information system for large-scale public transportation within metropolitan areas.
⑤ The Director of the Metropolitan Transportation Economics Division is responsible for the following matters: <Revised on 2022.2.22>
1. Matters related to the basic fare standards for large-scale public transportation within metropolitan areas.
2. Matters related to the method of calculating integrated fares for large-scale public transportation within metropolitan areas.
3. Matters related to data sharing and utilization between relevant institutions regarding integrated fares for large-scale public transportation within metropolitan areas.
4. Metropolitan area transportation cards.

Items related to the establishment and expansion of a fare settlement system based on data utilization.
5. Matters related to the operation of regular and discounted public transportation passes in metropolitan areas, as well as measures to reduce transportation costs.
6. Matters related to the determination of fare standards and rates for metropolitan area public transportation.
6.2. Matters related to the establishment of fare standards and rates for inter-city public transportation transfers in metropolitan areas.
7. Matters related to the designation, modification, and adjustment of taxi service areas in metropolitan areas.
8. Matters related to the composition and operation of the taxi transportation review and adjustment committee in metropolitan areas.
9. Matters related to coordination and dispute resolution involving transportation operators, railway companies, and other entities in metropolitan areas.
10. Matters related to the analysis of metropolitan area transportation databases and related policies.
10.2. Matters related to support projects for promoting public transportation utilization by utilizing transportation data such as transportation cards, pedestrian, and bicycle usage data.
11. Matters related to transportation surveys and transportation demand analysis in metropolitan areas.
12. Matters related to the establishment and operation of a metropolitan area integrated big data platform for transportation.
13. Matters related to the provision of metropolitan area transportation information and support for related industries.

Regarding the following matters:

14. Establishing, managing, analyzing, and utilizing transportation statistics related to regional transportation infrastructure, transportation businesses, and users within metropolitan areas.
15. Technical development and promotion of regional mobility within metropolitan areas.
16. Development and deployment of demand-responsive regional transportation services.
17. Establishing and operating integrated transportation services (MaaS) for metropolitan areas.
18. Research and evaluation of the level of regional transportation services within metropolitan areas.
